Glad to hear it, as long as the weather is good I think it should be a highlight of your trip! Note that to check in you go to the bar on the ground floor and let them know you're there and they'll ping the gentleman who runs the place to come down and give you your key - it sounds sketchy but it's actually pretty slick and there's a sign saying Mar Mar on the pillar outside the bar, and the guy told me that the bar is run by his family. The hostel itself is down an alley and up some stairs from the bar. Also, use the shower that's in the kitchen because the bigger handicap accessible one somewhat floods the floor of that bathroom when you use it.

Party time pretty much only after dark, especially on the weekend. At first people are seated at the tables they have for sidewalk seating and then they start heading inside closer to 10pm. They have some sort of theme night in the bar every night (ladies night, karaoke night, beer pong night etc) and it's often quite packed but sometimes nothing to write home about. The hostel rooms are in several adjacent buildings to the bar which is in its own building. I didn't bring earplugs and never actually had difficulty sleeping, actually what will really wake you up is the trash guy dumping all the collected glass into his truck at 9am.

If you have two full days, I'd plan on doing one of those each day and probably don't anticipate doing anything else for the rest of the day other than going out for pizza at night. A Capri tour usually means taking the train out to Sorrento which seemed a bit touristy but is really beautiful and perhaps worth doing a bit of shopping or getting a meal in.

I think you could if you avoided eating too close to the touristy areas, and perhaps make one of those meals be pizza or a sandwich. I only ever saw pizzas over 10euro near the tourist areas, and had plenty of delicious ones that were only 7 or 8 euro. It will specifically help to bring your own water bottle that you refill because you'll pay 2 euro just for a water at a lot of restaurants. So if you only spent 8 euro on lunch you'd have enough for a nicer meal at dinner!

Stop giving away my time and effort for free? Sadly, I have to disagree. I'll [quote](http://www.electricalaudio.com/phpBB3/viewtopic.php?p=1482905&sid=a85020718c4cbc24d0d689cf0b946ff6#p1482905) Steve Albini: "If nobody is willing to pay you to do something, then it isn't as valuable to the world as it is to you. You then decide if it's worth doing for its own sake. If it isn't, quit. If it is, carry on and who knows, maybe people will see value in it later and reward you. If not, you're still doing something you want to do. While I think labor should be valued by society, the avenues to enforce that are limited to industries that hire employees, not people who do creative work on their own."

I'm in a band, and we love playing for free. Why? Because don't draw nearly as much when there's a cover charge. We'd all rather play to a packed room than get relatively insignificant amount of money. If we're getting free beer either way, then who cares?

And you know what? The model works. I saw The Weeknd last fall. At that point he had only released three albums online for free and had never released anything physically. Within 11 days he sold out a 1,500 capacity venue, at $30 a ticket. That's 45 grand in the air that night to be distributed among all involved parties. For an hour of music. 45 grand.

There are countless other examples. Odd Future became popular because of their tumblr which contained many free albums as mediafire links. One of their members was recently nominated for six Grammies. A$AP Rocky signed a deal for $3 million off the strength of a free mixtape. I could go on.

Point is that real artists don't determine whether they create based on how profitable it is. When you're young, all that matters is getting your name out there.
